slaAccess.boundaryTitle: Credential boundary: one-time token for long-lived credentials, no admin password in the deployment
slaAccess.boundaryDesc: SLA accounts are service principals, not people: an administrator issues a one-time bootstrap token here (15 minutes by default, shown once), the SLA deployment exchanges it for long-lived refresh credentials and renews them on its own. The credentials are read-only (SLA_READONLY) or read plus configuration writes (SLA_OPERATOR); they never include account or permission management, API key management, or call-history bodies.
slaAccess.accountsHint: "Active credentials" = refresh tokens not yet revoked; "Unused tokens" = bootstrap tokens issued but not consumed
slaAccess.emptyHint: Create an account with a role template first, then issue a one-time bootstrap token for it and put that token into the SLA deployment configuration.
slaAccess.issueDesc: The token is shown only once and becomes useless as soon as it is consumed. You may bind it to a source IP: requests from other addresses are rejected even with the token.
slaAccess.issueTtlHint: 15 minutes by default, enough to paste it into the deployment config
slaAccess.issueIpPlaceholder: Leave empty to allow any source
slaAccess.issueResultDesc: Copy it into SLA_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN now; the SLA deployment exchanges it for long-lived credentials on startup.
slaAccess.copyFailed: Copy failed, select and copy manually
slaAccess.enableConfirm: Enabling only restores the account switch; the login principal is not restored automatically. Issue a new bootstrap token before the SLA can reconnect.
slaAccess.disableConfirm: Disabling revokes every credential and suspends the login principal, so issued access tokens stop working immediately. To reconnect later, enable the account and issue a new token.
slaAccess.enableSuccess: Account enabled; issue a new bootstrap token to reconnect
slaAccess.revokeConfirm: Revoking invalidates every refresh credential of this account immediately; the SLA stops reporting until a new token is issued.
slaAccess.deleteConfirm: Deleting also removes the credentials and the mirrored jwt_accounts row. This cannot be undone.
slaAccess.noMatchHint: Try another keyword, or clear the search box to see all accounts.
slaAccess.createRoleHint: SLA_READONLY is read-only; SLA_OPERATOR also has config write access (no user/permission management or audit writes).
